subject: ACME - Model routing & policy next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Shah <samir.shah@acme.com>, Lydia Chen <lydia.chen@acme.com>
Cc: dev.patel@redwood.ai, marcus.lin@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 25 Jun 2026 16:10:00 -0700
Subject: ACME - Post-call recap & next steps (model routing + policy)

Hi Samir / Lydia —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap of what we aligned on and proposed next steps so everyone is on the same page.

Summary of needs (from the call):
- Multi-tier routing: low-latency model for chat, cost-efficient large-batch reranking for nightly jobs.
- Region-aware routing (US primary, EU fallback).
- Fallback chains for capacity / cost (e.g., gptx-lowlat -> gptx-cost -> open-compat).
- Auth + onboarding: SDK key-based auth for devs, SSO for production admins.
- Structured output & tool-calling for the agent prototype; embeddings + reranker for search result re-ranking.

Action items we committed to:
1) I’ll send a short RFC + suggested policy config and a one-page integration checklist (SDK, auth, example routing policy).
2) Technical sync: Marissa + Dev + Marcus to run through SDK auth and a sample routing config with your infra team.
3) Pricing / procurement: Marissa to share a draft SOW for committed capacity and related timelines.

Attachments: I’m attaching a 1-page proposal that maps routes to latency/cost tiers.

Next steps (proposed):
- Samir: confirm availability for a 45-min technical sync next week (please share 2 windows).
- Lydia: loop in procurement if you want the SOW early for budget planning.

Thanks — talk soon.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood-routing-proposal.pdf (application/pdf, 1 page)]

Thanks Marissa — useful summary. A few follow-ups from our side before the tech sync:

1) Auth: for the PoC we prefer API keys scoped per environment. For production we need SSO integration (Okta) + centralized key rotation. Do you have an SSO SAML flow doc?

2) Failover priorities: in the example fallback chain you mentioned cost-first vs latency-first — can you provide recommended defaults we should start with?

3) Embeddings / reranker: would like to confirm that embeddings can be generated in-region (EU) for GDPR-sensitive datasets, and that reranker can call an on-prem model if needed.

4) Can you share the SDK quickstart and a sample routing policy snippet we can drop into our staging deployment?

Availability: next Tue/Wed afternoons PT work for our infra folks — prefer Wed 11am PT.

Samir

Date: Fri, 26 Jun 2026 09:20:00 -0700
Subject: RE: ACME - Post-call recap & next steps (model routing + policy)

Hi Samir —

Great questions — answers inline below and a couple of attachments to help the PoC: redwood-routing-proposal.pdf (attached) and a SOW draft for procurement.

1) Auth / SSO: we support API keys scoped by environment today and have an SSO SAML flow for enterprise admins (Okta). I’m attaching our SSO checklist and an integration doc excerpt. For PoC, API keys are easiest; for production we’ll help with SAML metadata exchange.

2) Fallback defaults: recommended starter policy:
- latency-first route: route to redwood/gptx-lowlat (p99 < 300ms)
- cost-safety fallback: if queueing exceeds threshold or model unavailable, fail over to redwood/gptx-cost (quantized)
- open fallback: if both dedicated models unavailable, route to open/gpt-compat (best-effort)

We’ll provide a sample JSON policy you can copy into staging.

3) Embeddings in-region: yes — embeddings jobs can be pinned to region (EU) to keep vectors in-region. Reranker can call either hosted reranker or a customer-on-prem model via a bridge; we’ll sketch both options in the tech sync.

4) SDK + sample policy: quickstart gist here: https://gist.github.com/dev_patel/quickstart-sdk-example — contains auth examples and a routing policy snippet. Also linking a shared drive folder with the RFC and SOW: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3c-redwood-acme-arch

Proposed tech sync: Wed Jul 1, 2026 at 11:00am PT. If that works, we’ll send a calendar invite and agenda.

Next steps from our side:
- Marissa: send SOW draft and proposal (attached).
- Dev: prepare SDK demo that shows region pinning and a fallback chain in the router.
- Marcus: bring a short overview of structured output/tool-calling + embeddings/reranker options.

Let me know if Wed 11am PT works and I’ll schedule.

Thanks —
Marissa
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
[Attachments: redwood-routing-proposal.pdf, acme-sow-draft.docx]
